title: Delivery of Proteins, Peptides or Cell-impermeable Small Molecules into Live Cells by Incubation with the Endosomolytic Reagent dfTAT
protocol: Swell 500 mg of rink amide MBHA resin in dimethylformamide (DMF) for 1 hour.
Incubate the Fmoc-protected resin in a 20% piperidine solution twice, with a washing step using DMF between reactions.
Deprotect the resin by rinsing multiple times with approximately 150 ml of DMF and removing the solvent by vacuum filtration after each incubation.
Synthesize CK(TMR)RKKRRQRRRG (fTAT) on the rink amide MBHA resin.
Use Fmoc-protected amino acids: Fmoc-Lys(Mtt)-OH, Fmoc-Lys(Boc)-OH, Fmoc-Gly-OH, Fmoc-Arg(Pbf)-OH, Fmoc-Gln(Trt)-OH, and Fmoc-Cys(Trt)-OH for the synthesis.
Perform each amino acid coupling reaction for 4 hours using HBTU and diisopropylethylamine dissolved in DMF under N2 agitation at room temperature.
Wash the resin with DMF following each coupling reaction.
Deprotect the resin after each coupling as described previously.
Synthesize the linear peptide chain of fTAT: CKRKKRRQRRRG.
Wash the resin thoroughly with DMF.
Follow up by washing the resin with dichloromethane (DCM).
Remove solvent from the resin using vacuum filtration.
Confirm the molecular weight of the synthesized peptide using MALDI-TOF.
Prepare a matrix mix by adding 1 mg of α-Cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid to a solution composed of 50 µl of 0.01% TFA in water and 50 µl of acetonitrile.
Run an analytical HPLC of the crude peptide and collect 50 µl from the top of the pure peak.
Prepare the sample for MALDI plate by adding 8 µl of the peptide to 2 µl of the matrix solution.
Place the prepared sample on the MALDI plate to air dry or on a 37 °C heat plate.
Perform a Kaiser test to detect free amines remaining on the resin after coupling steps.
Repeat coupling steps if a blue color is detected in the Kaiser test, indicating uncoupled amino groups.
Cleave the Mtt protecting group at the -amino group of Lys on CK(-NH-Mtt)TATG with 1% TFA and 2% triisopropylsilane (TIS) in DCM.
Incubate the resin with 20 ml of MTT solution for 5 min until no yellow color is observed.
Wash the resin with DCM and DMF between incubations.
Add a solution containing 1% TFA in DCM (no TIS) to the resin to ensure no more MTT is removed and the solution remains clear.
Dissolve Carboxytetramethylrhodamine (TMR), HBTU, and DIEA in DMF at respective ratios of 4, 3.9, and 10 equivalents relative to the amount of resin (in mg).
Add this mixture to the resin under dry N2 for overnight reaction.
Wash the resin with DCM after Fmoc-deprotection and amino acid conjugation, then allow it to dry.
Add a solution containing 92.5% TFA, 2.5% H2O, 2.5% TIS, and 2.5% EDT (total volume = 4 ml) to the peptidyl-resin for 3 hr at RT for global deprotection and cleavage.
Drain the solution from step into 40 ml of cold anhydrous ethyl ether (Et2O).
Spin down the mixture at 4 °C and 4,000 x g for 20 - 25 min to precipitate crude peptide products.
Repeat this step with additional cold anhydrous Et2O washes as needed.
Resuspend precipitates in water until completely dissolved.
Lyophilize the products obtained.
Resuspend the lyophilized products in 0.1% aqueous TFA/acetonitrile.
Perform HPLC analysis using an analytical C18 column (5 µm, 4 x 150 mm) at a flow rate of 1 ml/min with detection at 214 nm and 550 nm.
Use linear gradients of 0.1% aqueous TFA (solvent A) and 90% acetonitrile, 9.9% water, and 0.1% TFA (solvent B).
Perform semi-preparative HPLC on a C18 10 x 250 mm column at a flow rate of 4 ml/min with detection at 214 nm and 550 nm.
Confirm peptide identity by MALDI-TOF according to manufacturer’s protocol using an α-cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid matrix.
Aerate phosphate buffered saline (PBS) pH 7.4 for 1 hour.
Dissolve fTAT (0.3 mg, 1.5 x 10^-4 mmol) in aerated PBS pH 7.4 (5 ml).
Adjust the pH to between 7.0 - 7.5 with sodium hydroxide if necessary.
Nutate the reaction overnight to allow it to react until completion.
Purify the product using reverse-phase HPLC.
Analyze the purified product by mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF).
Lyophilize pure dfTAT and resuspend in 200 μl water.
Resuspend an aliquot of purified dfTAT in a 149 µl of 50 mM TCEP solution.
Allow the sample to react for approximately 20 min.
Measure the absorbance at 556 nm using Beer’s Law.
Calculate the concentration of fTAT from the measured absorbance.
Determine the concentration of dfTAT by dividing [fTAT] by two.
Seed cells (HeLa, HDF, etc.) in a dish at a confluency of 80 - 90%.
Grow cells in an appropriate medium until they reach 80 - 90% confluency.
Maintain the cell culture in a 37 °C humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2.
Wash the cells three times with PBS.
Dilute dfTAT stock in nrL-15 media to make a 5 µM working concentration.
Incubate cells with 5 µM dfTAT and cargo at 37 °C for 1 hr.
Wash cells with heparin (1 mg/ml) in L-15.
Incubate cells with cell-impermeable nuclear stain, such as Sytox Blue or Sytox Green (2 µM in nrL-15), to determine whether the plasma membrane is compromised.
Image cells using a fluorescence microscope at 100X oil immersion or 20X objective.
Image dfTAT using a RFP filter with excitation = 560 ± 20 nm and emission = 630 ± 35 nm.
Assess successful delivery of the protein or peptide by observing diffuse fluorescence throughout the cell.
Use staining of nucleoli by fTAT as an indication that the fluorescence detected is intracellular.
Identify the “optimal delivery” concentration required to achieve efficient cytosolic release of dfTAT in the cell type used.
Perform fluorescence microscopy on cells incubated with increasing concentrations of dfTAT.
Define the optimal dfTAT concentration as the minimal concentration that leads to clear cytosolic “diffuse” TMR fluorescence in approximately 100% of cells in a culture.
Vary the concentration of MOI used in co-incubation protocol while keeping the concentration of dfTAT constant.
Consider changing the incubation time to less than 1 hour as an option to vary the amount of MOI delivered.
